CapCut Help Center: Standard vs Pro
CapCut Help Center: new subscription pricing

caption:
CapCut's AI can caption a video, turn a script into a first draft and cut a long video into shorts.
Here is how each one works, and which parts need Pro.

Which CapCut AI tool do you use most?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: CapCut · Photo: CapCut
threads_text: CapCut's AI does three useful things: auto captions, script to video and cutting long videos into shorts. CapCut's own help page lists auto captions as a Pro tool now. Would you pay for captions or type them yourself?

slides.headline: How to use *CapCut AI*: captions, scripts and clips in minutes

slides.heading: 1. Turn on *Auto captions*
paras: On desktop: import your video, open the Text tab, click Auto captions, pick the language and click Create.
The captions land on the timeline, ready to edit.

slides.heading: 2. Fix and *style* them
paras: Read every line. Accents, noise and names trip the AI up.
On the web, the Styles tab has looks like Glow, or let Style captions with AI pick one.

slides.heading: 3. Write a *script*, get a video
paras: In Script to video, pick Narration or Commercial, describe your idea and choose one of the scripts.
Click Generate video for a first draft built from stock footage.

slides.heading: 4. Cut a long video into *shorts*
paras: The AI Clip Maker finds highlights in a podcast or talk and cuts them into vertical clips.
Preview them, click Edit more if needed, then Export.

slides.hook: Follow for more AI tools explained in plain words.

site_article.headline: How to use CapCut AI: auto captions, AI video maker and clipper
site_article.dek: Step by step instructions for the three CapCut AI tools people use most, and what each one needs from your plan.
site_article.summary: CapCut's AI tools can add captions to a video, turn a script into a first draft and cut a long video into short clips. CapCut's help center lists auto captions among the Pro plan's AI tools, so check your plan before you start.
site_article.seo_title: How to use CapCut AI: captions, video maker and clipper
site_article.seo_description: How to use CapCut AI step by step: auto captions on desktop, web and phone, script to video, the AI Clip Maker for shorts, and what needs Pro.
site_article.answer_summary: To use CapCut AI captions on desktop, import a video, open the Text tab, click Auto captions, pick the language and click Create. Script to video and the AI Clip Maker work from CapCut's tools pages, and CapCut lists auto captions as a Pro feature.
site_article.hero_alt: CapCut promotional image for adding subtitles to a video.

paragraphs.text: If you want to know how to use CapCut AI, start with three tools. Auto captions writes subtitles from the speech in your video. Script to video writes a script from your idea and builds a first draft from stock footage. The AI Clip Maker finds the best moments in a long video and cuts them into short vertical clips. All three come from CapCut's own instructions below.

One thing first: money. CapCut's help center lists auto captions, AI avatars and AI generated content among the advanced AI tools of its Pro plan, while the cheaper Standard plan gets basics like noise reduction. Descript, which sells a competing editor, reports that CapCut moved auto captions behind a paid tier in a 2025 pricing change. CapCut says Pro now comes with 1,200 AI credits and 1TB of cloud storage, and that prices depend on your region and platform, so check the subscription page in the app before you plan around it.
How to add auto captions in CapCut

paragraphs.title: 1. On desktop: import your video
paragraphs.text: Open CapCut on your computer and start a new project. In the left sidebar, open the Import tab under Media and click Import, or drag your video into the workspace.

paragraphs.title: 2. Create the captions
paragraphs.text: Open the Text tab at the top and click Auto captions. In the pop up, choose the language spoken in the video and click Create. The captions appear on the timeline as separate text clips.

paragraphs.title: 3. Edit and style them
paragraphs.text: Use the right sidebar. Captions is where you fix the words. Text, Animation and Tracking control the font, size, layout and movement. When you are happy, click Export in the top right corner, set resolution, frame rate and format, and click Export again.

paragraphs.title: 4. On the web: use AI captions
paragraphs.text: On the CapCut web start page, find the You may want to try section and click AI captions. Upload a video from your computer or your CapCut cloud space. CapCut says the video has to be shorter than 20 minutes. The text shows up in the Subtitles tab, where you can edit, delete or add lines. The Styles tab has looks such as Glow, Trending and Aesthetic, or you can click Style captions with AI and let it choose. Then click Export, or Edit more to open the full editor.

paragraphs.title: 5. On your phone: tap Auto captions
paragraphs.text: In the mobile app, tap Auto captions on the main screen, pick a video or audio file and tap Add. Choose the language and a template style, then tap Generate. Tap Edit captions to fix the text and change fonts and animations, then tap Done and export or share.

Read every caption before you post. CapCut itself says accents, background noise and specialist words can need manual fixes, and names are the usual casualty. If your language is not offered, you can still type subtitles with the text tools and line them up by hand.
How to turn a script into a video

paragraphs.title: 1. Open Script to video
paragraphs.text: Sign in to CapCut and open the Script to video tool in your browser. Click Narration for a voice led script, or Commercial if you are selling a product or service, and describe what the video is about.

paragraphs.title: 2. Pick a script
paragraphs.text: The AI writer gives you five scripts. Pick the one closest to what you want.

paragraphs.title: Prompt: a short narration idea
paragraphs.text: A 45 second video for small business owners about three simple ways to answer customer emails faster. Friendly, plain words, one tip per scene, end with a short call to action.

paragraphs.title: 3. Generate and replace
paragraphs.text: Click Generate video. CapCut builds a first draft from stock footage. Open it in the multi track editor to swap clips for your own, adjust captions, transitions and the voiceover, and set the shape of the video. Then click Export, name the project, choose resolution, frame rate and format, and download it.

Be realistic about this one. A draft made of stock footage looks like a draft made of stock footage. It is a fast way to get timing and structure, and a poor way to get something that feels like yours. Replace at least the opening shots with your own material.
How to cut a long video into shorts with the AI Clip Maker

paragraphs.title: 1. Upload the long video
paragraphs.text: Upload from your computer, CapCut cloud, Google Drive or Dropbox, and keep the page open until the upload finishes. CapCut suggests the tool for video podcasts, lessons, commentary and speeches, where people talk on camera.

paragraphs.title: 2. Let it find the highlights
paragraphs.text: The AI Clip Maker picks the strongest moments and cuts them into short clips. CapCut says it can also crop a wide 16:9 video to vertical 9:16 while tracking the speaker, and add captions. Before you export, you can change clip length and apply templates.

paragraphs.title: 3. Check, edit, export
paragraphs.text: Click Preview to watch each clip. Click Edit more to trim or fix one in the editor. Click Export to save it or share it straight to social media.

The AI picks moments from speech, so a clip can start mid thought or end before the punchline. Watch the first and last three seconds of every clip and trim by hand. Those six seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching.
What CapCut AI is good at, and what it is not

CapCut AI is good at the boring parts of short video: getting words on screen, finding the clip worth posting and turning a wide video into a vertical one. It is weaker at judgment. It does not know which name it misheard, which joke landed or whether stock footage fits your brand. Use it to get to a first version fast, then spend your own time on the opening seconds and the captions, because that is where viewers decide.
